# US Stock Market Daily Close Report | 2026-09-11

*Data cutoff: 20:30 UTC / 4:30 p.m. ET. September 11 was a normal trading session. Prices are regular-session closes unless noted. Technical statistics are calculated from daily market bars; volume comparisons are versus the trailing 20-session average.*

## 0. One-sentence Executive Summary

U.S. equities rebounded after four consecutive declines, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.86%, the Dow 0.98%, and the Nasdaq Composite 0.96%, as crude oil retreated and headline CPI matched expectations. The tone was cautiously risk-on, but the hotter-than-expected monthly core CPI reading pushed September Fed hike odds sharply higher and kept the 10-year Treasury yield near 5%. Capital favored technology hardware, semiconductors, servers, networking and industrial electrification, while software, healthcare, utilities and speculative nuclear names lagged. Equal-weight participation was respectable, but small caps underperformed and the late-session fade showed that the rebound did not fully resolve macro-rate risk. **Market state today: oversold rebound within a high-level consolidation, led by AI infrastructure rather than broad software participation.**

---

- Nasdaq and S&P performance was similar, but semiconductor leadership was clearer: SOX +1.81% and SOXX +1.86%.
- Russell underperformance and its sub-100DMA position show that participation remains uneven.
- VIX’s fall to 15.84 confirms short-term relief, not capitulation.

## 2. Intraday Timeline

| Time | Market Development |
|---|---|
| Premarket | Futures were already higher as oil pulled back. At 8:30 a.m. ET, headline CPI matched forecasts, but core CPI was slightly hotter, increasing Fed-hike expectations. Oracle initially traded near $162 after strong cloud results; Adobe initially weakened. |
| Open | SPY opened around $765.8 and QQQ near $715.7. Server and networking names immediately led—Dell, HPE, SMCI and ANET—while Oracle’s earnings gap began fading. |
| Midday | SPY reached roughly $766 and QQQ $717 as oil remained lower. Semiconductors, industrial power equipment and AI infrastructure attracted buy-the-dip demand. IWM failed to match large-cap strength. |
| Afternoon/close | Gains narrowed into the bell: SPY closed $764.29 versus a $766.37 high. This was a rebound rather than a closing-range breakout. Oracle finished negative despite strong results, a clear sell-the-news signal. |
| After-hours | Major index ETFs were little changed through 4:30 p.m. ET. No reliable broad-market after-hours catalyst had emerged at the data cutoff. |

The primary driver was relief from lower oil rather than falling short-term yields. AP described the session as a rebound after four declines, with Brent falling nearly 3% while rate-hike expectations increased ([AP](https://apnews.com/article/8c3272812f5e9b9238c6a3301921c17a)).

## 3. Macro Environment

### 3.1 Treasury yields

| 10Y-30Y | +38.1 bps | Flattened ~3.6 bps | Long-end stress stopped worsening on the day |

The real-time rates dashboard showed the 10-year near 4.974% and the 30-year near 5.355% ([Reuters/Investing](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/factboxmajor-brokerages-forecasts-for-sp-500-index-in-2026-4895277)); the 2-year quote was approximately 4.596% ([Investing historical data](https://ca.investing.com/rates-bonds/u.s.-2-year-bond-yield-historical-data)).

- **4.5%, 4.6%, 4.7%:** all three former resistance zones have been decisively exceeded. The market’s active question is now whether 5% holds.
- A sustained 10-year break above 5% would raise the discount rate for long-duration software and speculative growth, especially companies without positive free cash flow.
- The curve flattened because the 2-year rose more than the 10-year. That fits a Fed-hike narrative rather than a clean growth acceleration.
- Deficits, oil-driven inflation, Treasury supply and disappointing buyback/auction dynamics remain sources of term-premium risk.

### 3.2 Fed rate expectations

The next FOMC meeting is September 15-16, with the statement at 2:00 p.m. ET and press conference at 2:30 p.m. on September 16 ([Federal Reserve calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2026-september.htm)).

- CME-implied odds were approximately **85% for a 25-bp hike** and 15% for no change after CPI, versus roughly 72% hike odds beforehand. Immediate post-release estimates briefly reached about 91%, illustrating intraday model differences ([Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/11/the-feds-big-inflation-test), [CME FedWatch](https://www.cmegroup.com/fedwatch)).
- Probability of a cut at the September meeting: effectively 0%.
- **Expected cuts during 2026:** none are implied by the near-term setup; instead, the market favors at least one hike. No reliable data available for a precise full-year number of hikes at the 20:30 UTC cutoff.
- Fed speakers are constrained by the pre-meeting blackout period; the decision, projections and Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference are the next major policy catalysts.

## 11. Rotation Assessment

**Selected classifications:** **oversold rebound; AI hardware uptrend; AI hardware high-level consolidation; breadth expansion incomplete; strong indices with weaker small-cap internals.**

- **Money flowed into:** servers, networking, CPUs, selected semiconductors, optical equipment, electrical infrastructure and construction.
- **Money flowed out of/avoided:** speculative nuclear, healthcare, utilities, cloud/software baskets and some cybersecurity names.
- **AI health:** healthy at the spending and backlog level, but investors are increasingly distinguishing revenue/backlog from free-cash-flow quality.

**Market conclusion today:** Friday’s rebound was credible enough to stop the four-day decline, but it was driven mainly by lower oil and concentrated AI-infrastructure strength rather than an improvement in the rate outlook. Semiconductors, servers, networking and electrical infrastructure showed strong demand, while software and small caps failed to confirm broad risk-on leadership. The 10-year yield near 5%, higher Fed-hike odds and weak consumer sentiment keep macro risk elevated. Oracle’s earnings reversal also shows that the market is demanding free-cash-flow proof, not merely AI backlog growth.

**Current market phase: sector rotation.**

**My operating bias:** neutral. Chasing vertically extended server, hardware or power names after double-digit moves carries unfavorable short-term risk/reward; orderly pullbacks, support tests and post-earnings stabilization provide cleaner information. Position control remains important ahead of the FOMC, while software, speculative nuclear and companies dependent on external financing require particular caution.

2. Whether SPY reclaims 767 and QQQ closes above 718.  
3. Whether SMH continues outperforming QQQ and NVDA begins participating.  
4. Whether IWM reclaims 291 and 296, confirming broader participation.  
5. Whether WTI remains near $100 or reverses back above $103-$105.

*This report is for market review and observation only and does not constitute personalized investment advice.*

# US Stock Market Daily Close Report | 2026-09-10

**Data cutoff:** Approximately 4:30 p.m. ET on Thursday, September 10, 2026. U.S. markets were open normally, and September 10 is the latest completed session. Regular-session prices are used unless explicitly labeled after-hours.

## 0. One-sentence Executive Summary

U.S. equities fell for a fourth consecutive session as the Iran-related oil shock pushed Brent to $107.63, WTI to $102.48 and the 10-year Treasury yield toward 4.94%, overwhelming an otherwise broadly in-line PPI report. The S&P 500 lost 0.6%, the Nasdaq Composite 0.7%, the Dow 0.6%, and the Russell 2000 1.0%, while semiconductors and crowded AI-infrastructure stocks suffered materially larger declines. Apple, communication services and selected software names provided isolated support, but weak small caps, equal weight, housing and AI hardware signaled deteriorating participation. **Market state today: risk-off, rising-rate pressure with AI-hardware good-news fatigue and weak internals.**

---

The latest independently reported S&P moving-average reference placed the 50-DMA near 7,598 and 200-DMA near 7,147 as of September 8. [StreetStats](https://streetstats.finance/markets/breadth-momentum)

**Interpretation**

- The S&P 500 is only about 2.7% below its August 13 record close, so the index remains in a broader high-level range rather than a confirmed bear trend.
- Nasdaq and QQQ underperformed the S&P because higher yields hit long-duration valuations and semiconductors sold off.
- Russell 2000 weakness shows that the session was not a healthy large-to-small-cap rotation.
- SOXX and SMH materially underperformed QQQ, ending the recent relative resilience of chips.
- VIX near 16.5 indicates orderly de-risking rather than panic; that also leaves room for volatility to rise if CPI or oil disappoints.

## 2. Intraday Timeline

Early after-hours quotes remain subject to change. The tape was a **failed buy-the-dip**, not a short squeeze. The late reversal also argues that the market preferred reducing exposure ahead of CPI rather than holding high-beta gains overnight.

---

## 3. Macro Environment

### 3.1 Treasury yields

| 10Y-30Y | Roughly +40 bp | Little changed to modestly flatter | Long-end yields remain unusually high, but the 10-year led Thursday’s shock |

AP reported the 10-year at 4.94%, up from 4.83% late Wednesday. An earlier Reuters-derived snapshot showed 4.922% for the 10-year and 5.351% for the 30-year; the difference reflects timing during a volatile session. **Level assessment**

- **4.50%, 4.60% and 4.70% have all been decisively exceeded.**
- A sustained 10-year yield around 4.9%-5.0% raises the discount rate for AI, software and speculative infrastructure stocks.
- The rise is being driven by an adverse combination of oil-led inflation, sturdy labor data, Treasury-supply/fiscal concerns and reduced expectations for policy easing—not safe-haven buying.

### 3.2 Fed rate expectations

CME-implied pricing shifted to approximately a **73% probability of a 25-bp rate increase** at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, up from 61% Wednesday. Consequently, the market is no longer primarily debating “cut versus no cut”; it is debating **hike versus hold**.
